question: What is the white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulphate and barium chloride?
solution:
The correct answer __**Barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulfate and barium chloride is barium sulfate.
 
• The chemical reaction is as follows:

**Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)**

 
• In this reaction, the sodium and chloride ions from each reactant switch places to form sodium chloride and barium sulfate.
 
• Barium sulfate is a white, insoluble precipitate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
